test_cases.test_name: Verify Continuous Temperature Monitoring and Recording Intervals
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System continuously monitors temperature in GMP storage areas and records readings at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational in all GMP storage areas.
System access credentials are available.

test_steps.action: Access the Environmental Monitoring System interface and navigate to the real-time monitoring view for a designated GMP storage area.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays current temperature readings for the selected storage area.

test_steps.action: Observe the temperature readings for a period of at least 10 minutes, noting the timestamps of each recorded reading.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are continuously updated and recorded at intervals of 5 minutes or less.

test_steps.action: Export the recorded data for the observed period from the system.
test_steps.expected_result: A data export file is generated containing temperature readings and their corresponding timestamps.

test_steps.action: Analyze the exported data to confirm the recording interval between consecutive temperature readings.
test_steps.expected_result: All consecutive temperature readings in the exported data are recorded at intervals of 5 minutes or less.

acceptance_criteria: The system continuously displays and records temperature readings.
The interval between consecutive recorded temperature readings does not exceed 5 minutes.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be accurate and complete.
Timestamps must be precise.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Alarm Generation and Notification Integration
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system generates alerts when temperature deviates ±2°C from setpoint and that alarm notifications integrate with the site paging system.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational.
A specific GMP storage area with a defined temperature setpoint is configured.
Site paging system is operational and configured for integration.
System access credentials are available.

test_steps.action: Identify a GMP storage area with a known temperature setpoint and its associated alarm thresholds (e.g., setpoint 20°C, alarm at 18°C and 22°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The setpoint and alarm thresholds for the selected storage area are clearly defined and accessible within the system.

test_steps.action: Manually adjust the temperature in the selected storage area to a value that is 2°C below the setpoint (e.g., 18°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The system detects the temperature deviation and generates an alarm.
data_to_capture: Actual temperature reading at alarm trigger

test_steps.action: Verify that an alarm notification is received on the site paging system within the specified response time.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm notification is received on the site paging system, indicating the temperature deviation and the affected storage area.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of alarm notification on paging system

test_steps.action: Manually adjust the temperature in the selected storage area to a value that is 2°C above the setpoint (e.g., 22°C).
test_steps.expected_result: The system detects the temperature deviation and generates a second alarm.
data_to_capture: Actual temperature reading at alarm trigger

test_steps.action: Verify that a second alarm notification is received on the site paging system within the specified response time.
test_steps.expected_result: A second alarm notification is received on the site paging system, indicating the temperature deviation and the affected storage area.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of alarm notification on paging system

test_steps.action: Return the temperature in the storage area to within the acceptable range.
test_steps.expected_result: The system acknowledges the return to normal conditions and potentially clears the active alarms.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of temperature return to normal

acceptance_criteria: The system generates an alarm when temperature deviates ±2°C from the setpoint.
Alarm notifications are successfully sent to the site paging system.
Alarm notifications are received within the specified system response time (URS-EMS-011).
data_integrity_requirements: Alarm events must be accurately logged with timestamps.
Notification delivery must be reliable.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Range Accuracy and Data Storage Format
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS accurately monitors temperature within the specified range and that data is stored in the vendor's standard database format.
prerequisites: EMS is installed and configured.
Access to EMS software and database.
Calibrated temperature reference device.

test_steps.action: Introduce a controlled temperature deviation within the specified range (-80°C to +50°C) to a sensor in a GMP storage area. Use a calibrated reference device to confirm the actual temperature.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS displays the introduced temperature reading, which matches the reference device within ±0.5°C.

test_steps.action: Access the EMS database and query for the recorded temperature data from the previous step.
test_steps.expected_result: The recorded temperature data is present in the vendor's standard database format, as confirmed by database schema or vendor documentation.

acceptance_criteria: All temperature readings recorded by the EMS are within ±0.5°C of the calibrated reference device.
Temperature data is stored in the vendor's standard database format.
data_integrity_requirements: Data accuracy within specified tolerance.
Data stored in a verifiable and standard format.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Audit Trail and Electronic Signature Functionality
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS maintains a comprehensive audit trail for all critical events and that electronic signatures are implemented using the vendor's built-in functionality.
prerequisites: EMS is installed and configured.
User accounts with appropriate permissions are created.
Access to EMS audit trail logs and electronic signature features.

test_steps.action: Perform a critical action within the EMS, such as changing a setpoint or acknowledging an alarm. Ensure this action requires an electronic signature.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an audit trail entry detailing the action, the user who performed it, the date and time, and the reason for the action.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail entry generated in Step 1. Verify that an electronic signature was applied using the vendor's built-in functionality.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail entry clearly indicates the use of an electronic signature, including the signer's name, date, time, and the meaning of the signature, all generated by the vendor's standard functionality.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of electronic signature format and content

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify or delete the audit trail entry or electronic signature.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents any modification or deletion of the audit trail entry or electronic signature.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of immutability of audit trail and signature

acceptance_criteria: All critical events are logged in the audit trail with sufficient detail (who, what, when, why).
Electronic signatures are applied using the vendor's built-in functionality and meet 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.
Audit trail entries and electronic signatures are immutable.
data_integrity_requirements: Comprehensive and immutable audit trail.
Secure and compliant electronic signatures.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Standard Reports for Batch Release and Data Archival
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system utilizes vendor-supplied standard reports for batch release and that data archival functions correctly for the required retention period.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical data exists to test reporting and archival.
Access to vendor-supplied standard reports is available.
Archival feature is configured for 7 years retention.

test_steps.action: Access the EMS and generate a standard report for a specific batch or time period, as typically used for batch release.
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates a report using the vendor's standard report format. The report contains accurate historical temperature and humidity data for the selected period.

test_steps.action: Initiate the data archival process for data older than a specified period (e.g., simulating 7 years of data).
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully archives the specified historical data. The archival process completes without errors, and the archived data is inaccessible from the active system but retrievable via the archival feature.
data_to_capture: Verification of data unavailability in active system

test_steps.action: Attempt to retrieve archived data using the vendor's archival feature.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully retrieves the previously archived data, confirming the integrity and accessibility of the archived records.

acceptance_criteria: Vendor-supplied standard reports are used for batch release.
Generated reports accurately reflect the monitored environmental data.
Data archival process completes successfully.
Archived data is retained for the specified 7-year period.
Archived data is retrievable via the system's archival feature.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-007: Standard reports provided by vendor shall be used for batch release.
URS-EMS-010: Data shall be retained for 7 years using vendor's archival feature.
data_integrity_requirements: Data in reports must be accurate and complete.
Archived data must be preserved and retrievable without corruption.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Availability and Data Storage Capacity
test_cases.objective: To verify that the Environmental Monitoring System meets the specified availability target and has sufficient data storage capacity for the required 10-year period.
prerequisites: Environmental Monitoring System (EMS) is installed and configured.
System has been operational for a period to allow for availability monitoring (if applicable).
Access to system logs and monitoring tools for availability and storage usage.

test_steps.action: Monitor system uptime and record any unplanned downtime over a defined period (e.g., 1 month). Calculate the system availability percentage.
test_steps.expected_result: The calculated system availability percentage is 99.5% or higher, excluding documented planned maintenance periods.

test_steps.action: Review current data storage usage and estimate future growth based on monitoring intervals and data retention policies.
test_steps.expected_result: The current storage capacity is sufficient to support a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring, with adequate buffer for unexpected data volume increases.
data_to_capture: Estimated remaining storage capacity for 10 years

test_steps.action: Simulate a high data load scenario (if possible) by increasing the monitoring frequency temporarily or by introducing a large volume of historical data to assess storage performance.
test_steps.expected_result: The system continues to operate without performance degradation or data loss under simulated high data load conditions, and storage capacity is not exceeded prematurely.
data_to_capture: Storage performance metrics during high load
Data integrity checks after high load simulation

acceptance_criteria: System availability is 99.5% or greater, excluding planned maintenance.
Data storage capacity is sufficient for a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring.
System performance remains stable under high data load.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-012: Data storage capacity shall support minimum 10 years of continuous monitoring.
URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
data_integrity_requirements: Continuous monitoring requires high system availability to prevent data gaps.
Sufficient storage prevents data loss due to capacity exhaustion.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Response Time for Alarm Conditions
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system responds to alarm conditions within the specified time limit.
prerequisites: EMS system is fully installed and operational.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and functioning.
Alarm setpoints are configured correctly.
Site paging system is integrated and functional.

test_steps.action: Manually induce a temperature deviation that triggers an alarm condition in a monitored area.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm notification is generated by the EMS system.

test_steps.action: Measure the time elapsed from the moment the alarm condition is met to the moment the alarm notification is received by the site paging system.
test_steps.expected_result: The total response time for the alarm condition does not exceed 30 seconds.
data_to_capture: End time of alarm notification receipt.

test_steps.action: Document the measured response time and compare it against the URS-EMS-011 requirement.
test_steps.expected_result: The measured response time is less than or equal to 30 seconds.

acceptance_criteria: The system response time for alarm conditions is consistently within 30 seconds.
data_integrity_requirements: Accurate timestamping of alarm events.
Uncorrupted alarm notification data.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Integration with Facility Management System
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system successfully interfaces with the existing facility management system using standard protocols.
prerequisites: EMS system is fully installed and operational.
Facility Management System (FMS) is operational.
Network connectivity between EMS and FMS is established.
Details of the standard protocols for integration are available.

test_steps.action: Configure the EMS system to send temperature and humidity data to the FMS using the specified standard protocols.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS system is configured successfully without errors.

test_steps.action: Monitor the FMS to confirm receipt of temperature and humidity data from the EMS system.
test_steps.expected_result: The FMS receives and displays accurate temperature and humidity data from the EMS system.
data_to_capture: Screenshots of FMS displaying EMS data.
Sample data points from both systems for comparison.

test_steps.action: Verify that the data transmitted and received is consistent and accurate, comparing values between the EMS and FMS.
test_steps.expected_result: The data displayed in the FMS matches the data recorded by the EMS system within acceptable tolerances.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS system successfully transmits temperature and humidity data to the FMS.
Data received by the FMS is accurate and consistent with EMS readings.
data_integrity_requirements: Data transmitted between systems is not corrupted.
Data is accurately represented in both systems.

test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS accurately measures and records temperature within the specified range of -80°C to +50°C with an accuracy of ±0.5°C.
prerequisites: EMS is installed and configured.
Calibrated temperature probes are installed in GMP storage areas.
Access to EMS software and data logs.

test_steps.action: Introduce a calibrated reference thermometer into a GMP storage area alongside an EMS probe.
test_steps.expected_result: The reference thermometer displays a stable temperature reading.

test_steps.action: Allow the system to stabilize for at least 30 minutes and record EMS temperature readings at 5-minute intervals.
test_steps.expected_result: EMS temperature readings are recorded at the specified intervals.

test_steps.action: Compare the EMS temperature readings with the reference thermometer readings.
test_steps.expected_result: The difference between EMS readings and reference thermometer readings is within ±0.5°C.
data_to_capture: Comparison of EMS and reference readings

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 1-3 at various points within the specified temperature range (-80°C to +50°C) to ensure consistent accuracy.
test_steps.expected_result: Accuracy is maintained across the entire specified temperature range.
data_to_capture: All readings and deviations from multiple temperature points.

acceptance_criteria: All recorded EMS temperature readings are within ±0.5°C of the calibrated reference thermometer readings across the entire specified range.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be accurate and reliable.
Readings must be traceable to the calibrated reference thermometer.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Alarm Deviation Threshold and Notification Integration
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS generates alerts when temperature deviates ±2°C from the setpoint and that these notifications integrate correctly with the site paging system.
prerequisites: EMS is installed and configured with defined setpoints for GMP storage areas.
Site paging system is operational and configured to receive notifications from the EMS.
Access to EMS software and alarm logs.
Ability to safely and temporarily alter temperature in a GMP storage area.

test_steps.action: Identify a GMP storage area with a defined temperature setpoint and alarm deviation of ±2°C.
test_steps.expected_result: A storage area with a clear setpoint and alarm threshold is identified.

test_steps.action: Carefully adjust the temperature in the selected storage area to be 2°C above the setpoint.
test_steps.expected_result: The temperature in the storage area rises to 2°C above the setpoint.

test_steps.action: Observe the EMS for alarm generation and verify that an alert is triggered within 30 seconds.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm is generated by the EMS within 30 seconds of the temperature exceeding the threshold.

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification is successfully sent to the site paging system.
test_steps.expected_result: An alert is received on the designated paging device.

test_steps.action: Return the temperature to within the acceptable range and verify that the alarm clears and any associated notifications are updated.
test_steps.expected_result: The alarm status clears in the EMS and the paging system reflects the cleared alarm.

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 2-5 by decreasing the temperature to 2°C below the setpoint.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm is generated, notification is sent to the paging system, and the alarm clears upon temperature normalization.
data_to_capture: All readings and timestamps for the low temperature deviation test.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS generates an alarm within 30 seconds when temperature deviates ±2°C from the setpoint.
Alarm notifications are successfully transmitted to the site paging system.
Alarms clear appropriately when the temperature returns to the acceptable range.
data_integrity_requirements: Alarm events must be accurately logged with timestamps.
Notification delivery must be reliable.
